newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ to start using forex swaps from Nov 11.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ to start using forex swaps from Nov 11.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand said on Friday it planned to start using forex swaps from Monday. The move is to help smooth liquidity flows.
Details of swap transactions undertaken will be released on a weekly basis along with the fortnight ahead cash influence Forecasts.
The bank said in September it did not expect the move to have any impact on monetary policy or on the New Zealand dollar.

Currently, the bank uses a repo system where it buys or sells bills to manage daily cash flows. Initially at least, the swaps operations will be on a relatively small scale, the bank said in September.
The bank would typically buy or sell New Zealand dollars on the spot market and simultaneously agree to buy or sell New Zealand dollars forward at some future date.
It said it had been reviewing its instruments in the light of two recent developments.
The first was the elimination of the government's net foreign debt, which had significantly reduced the amount of foreign exchange business the Reserve Bank did.
The other was projected large budget surpluses, which had made the bank review how monetary policy might be run effectively in an environment where government securities played a smaller role.

One reason for using the new system was that the New Zealand foreign exchange market was one of the deepest and most liquid of New Zealand markets. Daily turnover is around US$8 billion daily, with some $6 billion of that transacted in the forwards market.
Entry into the swaps market will be conducted potentially at any time of the day, the bank said and it did not plan to reveal its operations which would be on a relatively small scale.
